preconditions.description: The number of points n is between 3 and 2000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(points) == n and all(isinstance(p, tuple) and len(p) == 2 for p in points)
preconditions.description: The input contains exactly n points, each represented as a tuple of two integers (x, y).

preconditions.expression: all(p1 != p2 for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n) for p1 in [points[i]] for p2 in [points[j]])
len(s) == n - 2 and all(c in {'L', 'R'} for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s has length n-2 and consists only of 'L' or 'R'.

preconditions.expression: all(not collinear(points[i], points[j], points[k]) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) for k in range(n) if i != j and j != k and i != k)
preconditions.description: No three points are collinear (implied by problem statement).

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (len(permutation) == n and all(1 <= p <= n for p in permutation) and len(set(permutation)) == n)
postconditions.description: If no valid permutation exists, output is '-1'. Otherwise, output is a permutation of integers from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: stdout != '-1' and is_non_self_intersecting(permutation, points) and is_winding(permutation, points, s)
postconditions.description: The output permutation, if valid, forms a non-self-intersecting polygonal line that matches the winding sequence s.
